newsitem.title: USA: Illinois Gov. in rare appearance as trial witness.
newsitem.headline: Illinois Gov. in rare appearance as trial witness.

text.p: An Illinois governor appeared as a witness in a criminal trial for the first time in 75 years Tuesday as Jim Edgar deflected questions about his involvement in an alleged welfare contract scam.

Leading off the defence case in the fraud and bribery trial of Management Services of Illinois Inc. and several of its executives, the 51-year-old Republican said he was unaware of the multimillion dollar contracts the company had with the state welfare department.
A sitting governor in Illinois last testified at a criminal trial in 1922.

Edgar admitted that Management Services was among his biggest campaign backers, contributing thousands of dollars to his successful 1994 run for governor. He also said he repaid the company for a $17,000 computer system it provided him.

Prosecutors have charged company executives with showering state employees with gifts and meals to win contracts and swindle the state out of more than $7 million. Edgar was not charged with any wrongdoing, although a mid-level manager in the state welfare department has pleaded guilty.
Lawyers for the company, which was hired to find welfare cheats, have argued that the firm may have profited from its contract with the state but did nothing wrong.

"With 60,000 (state) employees and a budget of $30 billion, I can't guarantee that every employee and every dollar is going to be spent in the best manner," Edgar told reporters outside court after two hours of low-key testimony.
"What I think is important is that when you find a problem, how do you handle it? We found a problem, we turned it over for investigation," he said.
Edgar was expected to make a decision in the coming weeks about whether to run for a third term as governor, take on Democratic Sen. Carol Moseley-Braun in 1998 or retire from politics.
"When I weigh my future this (trial) is not a factor whether I run for something or not," Edgar said.
